title: Auditing Disability Representation in Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model-generated image descriptions using paired Neutral Prompts (NP) and Disability-Contextualized Prompts (DP). Evaluating the outputs using text-based metrics (VADER for sentiment, Regard for social respectfulness, Verbosity) and an LLM-as-judge framework to detect unsupported interpretive shifts, stereotyping, and deficit-oriented framing across 9 disability categories.

Analyzing intersectional and group-level demographic divergence by systematically varying the perceived gender of individuals in the synthetic paired images (PAIRS dataset) and measuring the resulting differences in interpretation shift, stereotyping, and framing under disability-contextualized prompts.

Analyzing intersectional and group-level demographic divergence by systematically varying the perceived race of individuals in the synthetic paired images (PAIRS dataset) and measuring the resulting differences in interpretation shift, stereotyping, and framing under disability-contextualized prompts.
